newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end 1.18 pct lower in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end 1.18 pct lower in slow trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed 1.18 percent lower in a lackluster session with a few local players dominating trade, brokers said.
"The volume is too thin, it is easy to manipulate and bring prices down," a trader said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 52 most traded shares ended down 770 points at 64,589 points. Turnover was a light 278 million reais ($272.4 million).
The market was also affected by a second-day strike which failed to close banks but interrupted the back-offices of some financial institutions, analysts said.
Traders shrugged off unconfirmed rumors reported by some local news agencies that Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola would resign.
"There is no news and this gives room for speculation," a broker said.
Benchmark Telebras preferred closed at 80.60 reais, a drop of 1.71 percent.
State power utility Eletrobras preferred fell 0.17 percent to 286 reais.
The Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index .IEE rose 0.11 percent, closing at 1,603 points.
